subject: Compact econ brief — quantization + batching packaging questions
messages:
From: Beth Carter <beth@maya.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@maya.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options — quant + batch guidance for pilot

Hi Dylan / Karthik,

Thanks again for the earlier demo — Maya AI loved the latency profile on the 8k LLM. We're preparing the internal pilot ask for a three-month evaluation and need a clearer read on the Optimize toolkit packaging so we can present to procurement. Two quick asks: 

1) If we pick the "compact" pilot (single-app, 50k monthly queries with 95th pct < 150ms target), what quantization recommendations do you make for LLMs like the ones you showed? Which variants preserve quality for our classification+short generation mix?

2) How does batch size and KV cache settings affect both the committed-credits economics and the ability to keep tail latency under the 150ms SLO? We need a simple mapping we can show to engineering and finance (e.g., pilot band X => batching profile Y => expected token unit cost).

We have a rough budget and will need conservative numbers. Can you share a short written summary and any sample scenario workbook?

Appreciate it —
Beth
Director of Product
Maya AI

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth@maya.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options — quant + batch guidance for pilot

Hi Beth — thanks for the concise asks. Looping in Monica (solutions lead) to align pricing/credits. Below is a compact summary we can present to procurement; attaching a scenario workbook once we finalize the banding.

Quick summary (compact pilot — 50k queries/month):
- Quantization: start with 8-bit PTQ for generation paths and 4-bit (Q4) for classification-heavy routes. Q4 preserves classification scores while 8-bit keeps free-text quality for short responses. We recommend A/B early in pilot: keep both variants available and route by endpoint.
- Batching & KV cache: enable request-level batching with max batch size 8 for gen endpoints and continuous KV cache for chat-like flows. This yields ~18–25% token-cost savings vs single-shot calls while keeping 95th pct latency within ~120–160ms depending on sequence length.
- Econ mapping (conservative):
  * Baseline (no batch, no cache) — unit token cost = 1.0x (reference)
  * Batch(8) + KV cache — unit token cost = 0.78x (approx)
  * Q4 (classification routes) + batch(4) — unit token cost = 0.62x

Caveats: hit rates on KV cache and tail token lengths matter — we included sensitivity in the workbook.

Next steps: Monica will share a conservative credits-based price band and an example workbook you can drop into procurement. If you want, we can include a guardrail that automatically falls back to hosted variants if latency spikes.

Best —
Dylan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Hi team — this is exactly the level we need. A couple of clarifying questions before procurement: 

- The econ mapping numbers you provided — are those inclusive of model hosting fees or just the Optimize toolkit adjustments (batching/quant benefits)? Procurement needs explicit line items for hosting vs optimization credits.
- For the fallback guardrail: can you give an example SLA/penalty-free behavior? We want to understand the operational implications if we hit a capacity ceiling.

Also — can Monica include a conservative scenario where KV cache hit rate is low (e.g., 20%)? That’s likely for our ephemeral query set.

Thanks — Beth

Hi Beth — attaching two quick artifacts: 1) "Optimizer_Econ_Scenarios.xlsx" (conservative/central/aggressive bands with explicit hosting vs Optimize-toolkit credit lines) and 2) "Quantization_Profile_v2.pdf" (recommended model variants and quality notes).

Short answers to your clarifying asks:
- Econ mapping: the workbook separates line items — hosting (model runtime + GPU hours), storage (KV cache storage), and Optimize toolkit credits (batching/auto-cache/quantization advisory features). The unit multipliers Dylan mentioned are the net effect on token-unit cost when you apply Optimize credits — the workbook shows the raw hosting cost and the post-optimization cost.
- Fallback guardrail: by default we propose an automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant in the same region when Dedicated capacity hits 95% utilization for >3 minutes. That route preserves availability but will degrade unit economics (we flag this as a "no-penalty" operational behavior in pilot). If you want contractual SLAs around fallback behavior, we can add an SLA appendix but that will affect pricing.
- Low KV hit scenario: included a 20% hit-rate pessimistic sheet — in that band net savings drop roughly 9–12% vs the central assumption. We recommend a short engineering pass to identify high-reuse prefixes to improve hit-rates during the pilot.

If this looks good, Dylan will issue a pilot quote (credits + hosting estimate) and we can route to procurement. Happy to hop on a 30-min call next week if you want us to walk through the workbook row-by-row.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

- Optimizer_Econ_Scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet, 320KB)
